criterion: The birthday finder presents its day field and month field as one labelled group rather than two anonymous boxes, and the result appears below with the content above holding still.
evaluation_rule: Tab into the finder. If the two fields announce as one labelled group and the result lands below without the story above shifting, that is a yes. A no is two unlabelled boxes, or content that jumps when the sixteen characters arrive.

criterion: Each route paints its own ground, ink and accent, so the home document, the hub, the passport scene and the prize machine read as four different worlds.
evaluation_rule: Open the home document, the hub, the passport scene and the prize machine in turn. Four visibly different grounds and accents is a yes. One palette carried unchanged across them is a no.

criterion: The hub presents its ten covers as a ring seen in perspective, with the selected cover square to the reader and its neighbours turned away.
evaluation_rule: A no here is a flat grid or a plain list of ten covers. Say yes only where the hub reads as a ring in perspective with one cover square to the reader and its neighbours turned away.

criterion: The arcade routes carry a neon character where the ceremonial routes carry a serif one, so the two registers read as products of one design system.
evaluation_rule: Compare an arcade route against a ceremonial one. Different type register, shared control shapes: yes. Indistinguishable routes, or two products that share nothing: no.

criterion: A character kept on the device appears in the collection immediately, marked as kept, and is visibly distinguishable from one merely resolved.
evaluation_rule: Keep a character and watch the collection. Yes when the entry changes appearance at once and is distinguishable from a merely resolved one; no when kept and unkept look the same.

criterion: The collection view stays responsive with several hundred entries, drawing what is in view rather than every character at once.
evaluation_rule: Scroll a collection of several hundred entries. Smooth travel is a yes. Stalling, or a first paint that waits on every character, is a no.

criterion: A game's end state reports the attempt against the reader's own best for that game, and says in words when the run was the first.
evaluation_rule: Finish a run twice. If the second end state names the earlier best and the first run was marked as a first, answer yes. A bare number both times is a no.

criterion: Each of the ten games presents a start control, a live readout and an end state in the same places, so the arcade reads as one machine rather than ten.
evaluation_rule: Walk three games and look at where the start control, the readout and the end state sit. Consistent placement earns a yes; three different layouts is a no.

criterion: Each screen of the hub and the game routes leads with one action that outweighs every other control on that screen.
evaluation_rule: On the hub and on a game route, one action should carry more visual weight than anything beside it. Where several controls compete equally, answer no; otherwise yes.

criterion: Empty, loading and refused surfaces are designed: an empty collection names what to do, and a refused date names what is impossible.
evaluation_rule: Empty the collection and submit an impossible date. Yes if each surface says what to do next in its own words. No if either is blank, or reaches for a generic message.

criterion: The sixteen series labels and the resolved characters are laid out so a reader can tell which character belongs to which series at a glance.
evaluation_rule: Resolve a date and look at the sixteen results. Yes when each character is visibly tied to its series; no when they read as an undifferentiated row.

criterion: The prize machine reads as a dark cabinet with its own typographic voice, distinct from the home document's warm ground.
evaluation_rule: The prize machine should not look like the home document. A dark cabinet with its own typographic voice is a yes; the home palette carried over unchanged is a no.

criterion: Movement on the hub carousel and the birthday finder overshoots its target slightly and settles, so arrivals feel springy rather than linear.
evaluation_rule: Watch a cover move and the finder resolve. A slight overshoot that settles earns a yes. Linear travel, or no movement at all, is a no.

criterion: Idle movement on the chrome is gentle and finite rather than a perpetual pulse at the edge of vision.
evaluation_rule: Sit on a route for half a minute without touching anything. Gentle motion that ends is a yes; something pulsing at the edge of vision without end is a no.

criterion: Every control on the home route and inside a game shows a visible focus indicator against that route's own ground when reached by keyboard.
evaluation_rule: Tab through the home route and through a game with the pointer away. Yes when the ring stays legible on every ground; no when focus vanishes on a saturated or dark route.

criterion: Every state that carries meaning in a game is conveyed by shape, position or text beside its colour.
evaluation_rule: Find a state the game signals in colour. If shape, position or wording carries it too, answer yes. If hue is the only difference, answer no.

criterion: At a narrow viewport the home route reflows to a single column and the hub becomes a swipe, with sideways scrolling confined to the hub itself.
evaluation_rule: Narrow the window until the home route is one column. Yes when it reflows cleanly and only the hub travels sideways; no when the page itself scrolls sideways.

criterion: The prize machine asks to be turned sideways at a narrow viewport and recovers by itself once the device is rotated.
evaluation_rule: Narrow the prize machine. The request to turn the device should appear, and clear on its own once rotated: that is a yes. A request that persists, or never appears, is a no.
